title: SN1: hydrolysis of 2-bromo-2-methylpropane
caption: Step 1 is slow: the C–Br bond breaks on its own, leaving a flat tertiary carbocation and bromide. Water attacks the carbocation (step 2), and a second water molecule removes a proton from the oxonium ion (step 3). Only the haloalkane is involved in the slow, rate-determining step, so rate = k[R–X].
alt: SN1 mechanism: 2-bromo-2-methylpropane ionises to a tertiary carbocation, water attacks it, and loss of a proton gives 2-methylpropan-2-ol.
description: Stage 1: 2-bromo-2-methylpropane, a central carbon with three methyl groups and a bromine. A curly arrow goes from the C–Br bond to the bromine. The reaction is in water.

Stage 2: the tertiary carbocation, a positive central carbon with three methyl groups in a flat arrangement, and a bromide ion. A curly arrow goes from a lone pair on the oxygen of a water molecule to the positive carbon.

Stage 3: an oxonium ion, the central carbon bonded to an OH₂⁺ group. A curly arrow goes from a lone pair on a second water molecule to one hydrogen of the OH₂⁺ group, and another from that O–H bond onto the oxygen.
Stage 4: 2-methylpropan-2-ol, a hydronium ion H₃O⁺ and a bromide ion.
